_note: The crab every player steers, its shell in the player's colour (SECOND-ORDER R1.90). Anatomy of a green or blue shore crab, checked from above, the side, the front and 3/4: a carapace wider than long (476 mm across the teeth, 452 behind them, 361 long), widest across its front third just behind the eyes, five teeth on each front-side margin, tapering to a narrower back edge, gently domed; two eyes on short stalks in notches at the front middle, short antennae between them; two claws from the front corners under the shell, each an arm (merus), a wrist (carpus) and a big palm (propodus, 156 mm long, 118 deep and up to 110 broad, a swollen teardrop section; the heaviest limbs) with a stout toothed fixed finger below and a movable finger (dactyl) hinged on top, folded in front of the face with the palms turned 22 degrees in (idle, walks, jump; hold, grab and place turn them straight so a held tile sits square); four pairs of walking legs from under the sides, splayed sideways (about 790 mm tip to tip), the upper segment (merus) flattened and broad, each rising from under the margin to a high knee above the shell and angling down to a pointed tip, bending in the plane across the body, the back pair swept back with paddle-flat tips as a swimming crab's; the abdomen a broad rounded flap folded flat under the body, one tile (200 mm) wide. Parts: body; eye_l, eye_r; claw_l_arm, claw_l_wrist, claw_l_palm, claw_l_finger and claw_r_...; leg_l1_hip, leg_l1_knee, leg_l1_foot for left legs 1 (front) to 4 (back) and leg_r1_... on the right, each named after the joint it turns about (hip: coxa and merus up to the knee; knee: carpus and propodus down to the ankle; foot: the dactyl). Anchors claw_left and claw_right: the middle of a held tile's underside, the tile's near edge between the open fingers (a 45 mm gap at rest). The walks go toward +x (walk_side) and +z (walk_fwd); played backwards they go the other way. The jump is the crab's pose only; the game lifts it. Written by tools/models/crab.py.
name: Crab
